therapy\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETo arrive at a diagnosis,for chronic headache CT or MRI is the preferred investigation of choice,MRI was done and talk\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ec)\u003C\/b\u003E What is the efficacy of each of the drugs listed in her prior treatment plan that she was following since last two years before she stopped it two weeks back?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFor example:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhy was she given bisphosphonates?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhat is the efficacy of using primary bisphosphonate prophylaxis for patients started on corticosteroids?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhat is the efficacy of using primary PPI prophylaxis during initiation of any corticosteroids to prevent Gi ulcers?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E___ Hydroxychloroquine,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Esulfasalazine,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Emethylprednisolone,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eaceclofenac\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Echolecalciferol,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ealandronic acid,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;flupirtine ,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Egabapentin ,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Emethylcobalamine tablets.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003EHydroxychloroquine\u003C\/u\u003E in SLE\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E“Chloroquine, together with its hydroxyl derivative hydroxychloroquine, was initially used as an antimalarial agent, but is also useful in the treatment of autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChloroquine and hydroxychloroquine are approved for the treatment of SLE and have been shown to reduce the frequency of disease flares (particularly of lupus nephritis), contribute to the maintenance of remission, prolong the onset of disease and reduce the risk of complications.Beyond their immunomodulatory effects in SLE, these agents have also been shown to protect against thrombotic events, improve glucose and lipid profiles, and prevent renal damage,apparently resulting in reduced cardiovascular risk, for which SLE is an independent risk factor”\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7097534\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7097534\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003ESulfasalazine\u003C\/u\u003E:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EImmunosuppressive drug used in the treatment of cutaneous manifestations of lupus.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E“Sulfasalazine is an effective agent for chronic discoid lupus erythematosus (CDLE) but the response to treatment is considerably variable between patients and is also unpredictable. The reason for this might relate to differences in metabolism of the drug which is extensively acetylated by the polymorphic enzyme N-acetyltransferase 2 (NAT2). To test this possibility, the N-acetylation phenotype of eleven patients with CDLE and treated by standard doses of sulfasalazine was retrospectively determined by genotyping. A clear-cut difference in the outcome of treatment was observed according to whether the patients were slow acetylators (SA) or rapid acetylators (RA). Eight out of 11 patients responded to treatment with a complete or marked remission of the disease. Seven of them were RA. The three other patients who did not respond at all to the drug were SA. In addition, SA seem to be more prone to toxic events. These findings strongly suggest that the genetic polymorphism of NAT2 is responsible for differences in the response to sulfasalazine in patients with CDLE. Therefore, candidates for sulfasalazine therapy should be genotyped to identify those patients who might benefit from the drug.”\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/journals.lww.com\/jpharmacogenetics\/Abstract\/1997\/04000\/NAT2_genotyping_and_efficacy_of_sulfasalazine_in.6.aspx\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/journals.lww.com\/jpharmacogenetics\/Abstract\/1997\/04000\/NAT2_genotyping_and_efficacy_of_sulfasalazine_in.6.aspx\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003EMethyl prednisolone\u003C\/u\u003E:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Glucocorticoids (GCs) are the mainstay of treatment of SLE as induction therapy and to manage acute flares and have dramatically improved the prognosis of severe SLE.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIntravenous (IV) pulse methylprednisolone therapy, mostly 500-1,000 mg daily for 1-3 days, was introduced in the 1970s (Cathcart, 1976) and is remarkably efficacious in critically ill patients (Isenberg, 1982), suffering renal impairment, central nervous system disease, severe arthritis, pleuropericarditis or thrombopenia.There is still a doubt\u0026nbsp; regarding\u0026nbsp; tapering of the dose of IV methylprednisolone needed to achieve rapid control of activity .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETapering schedules are mainly based on physician’s experience and clinical judgment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;In patients requiring the therapy adequate prevention of bone loss should be applied, keeping in mind that GC-induced osteoporosis is an early event. Patients must be immunized against influenza (every year) and Streptococcus pneumoniae (every 5 years)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.eular.org\/sysModules\/sysFiles\/ckeditor_4\/plugins\/doksoft_uploader\/userfiles\/18_main_CH21.docx_1.pdf\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.eular.org\/sysModules\/sysFiles\/ckeditor_4\/plugins\/doksoft_uploader\/userfiles\/18_main_CH21.docx_1.pdf\u003C\/a\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003EAceclofenac\u003C\/u\u003E:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E“The therapeutic effect of NSAIDs is determined by the suppressed\u0026nbsp; activity of the cyclooxygenase (COX) isoenzymes COX- 1 and COX-2. The widely use of NSAIDs in clinical practice is considerably limited by the risk of adverse reactions (ARs) in the gastrointestinal tract\u0026nbsp; (GIT), which are characteristic for this class of drugs. Medications\u0026nbsp; that are able to selectively inhibit the activity of COX-2 while\u0026nbsp; maintaining that of COX-1 less rarely cause ARs in GIT. This selective effect is produced by aceclofenac. The drug has been also noted to be well\u0026nbsp; tolerated: the risk for aceclofenac- induced ARs in GIT is\u0026nbsp; substantially lower than that due to the use of the majority of other NSAIDs”.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/mrj.ima-press.net\/mrj\/article\/view\/811?locale=en_US\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/mrj.ima-press.net\/mrj\/article\/view\/811?locale=en_US\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cu\u003Echolecalciferol\u003C\/u\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;There is a protective\u0026nbsp; effect of Vitamin D on the immunological abnormalities associated with SLE including its association with downregulation of the T-cell response, proliferation of B-cells, and upregulation of Tregs.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5361443\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5361443\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003EAlandronic acid:\u003C\/u\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Efor the prevention and treatment of osteoporosis in Glucocorticoid ‐treated individuals without renal impairment\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1002\/acr.20568\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1002\/acr.20568\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003EFlupirtin\u003C\/u\u003E: used as an analgesic for chronic and acute pain\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ed\u003C\/b\u003E) Please share any reports around similar patients with SLE and TB meningitis?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETubercular meningitis (TBM) is a rare condition in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The aim of this study is to describe the clinical characteristics, possible risk factors, and outcomes of SLE patients with TBM.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn systematically reviewing medical records from10 SLE patients with TBM admitted to a hospital from December 2008 to December 2018. A total of 100 cases in the same period were randomly selected as controls from SLE inpatients without infection. In patients with TBM, the mean age at presentation was 35.2 years (range 19.8–45.2); the mean duration of SLE was 34.6 months (range 4–84 months). Patients with TBM had significantly longer SLE duration, higher ESR and CRP level, and lower CD4+ cell counts and albumin level than those without infections (p \u0026lt; 0.05 for all). There were no differences in prednisone dose at the time of symptom onset or cumulative dose over the preceding year between the two groups. Logistic regression analysis showed that patients with a lower CD4+ cell count were more likely to have TBM compared with controls (OR = 3.67, p = 0.020).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETBM should be considered when SLE patients have central nervous system (CNS) symptoms with a longer duration, higher ESR and CRP level, and lower CD4+ cell counts and albumin level, even if the patients are receiving a low prednisone dose,and the patient being studied has a chronic headache and fits into this criteria\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Source:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/link.springer.com\/article\/10.1007\/s10067-020-04940-9\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/link.springer.com\/article\/10.1007\/s10067-020-04940-9\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAny reports of normal csf leukocyte count and normal csf protein in meningitis?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhat could be the probable cause for a normal csf leukocyte count in a patient with chronic meningitis?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ee) What is the sensitivity and specificity of ANA in the diagnosis of SLE?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMethods\u003C\/b\u003E: Retrospective chart review in a 400-bed teaching hospital in which 1010 patients (including inpatients and outpatients) for whom ANA testing was ordered over 10 months; all patients with positive ANA test results and an equal number of randomly selected patients with negative test results were included. Clinical utility of the ANA in the identification of rheumatic disease was determined by its estimated sensitivity, specificity, and positive and negative predictive values.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EResults\u003C\/b\u003E: Of 1010 ANA test results reviewed, 153 were positive. The group with positive ANA test results included more patients aged 65 years or older than the group with negative ANA test results (30% vs 15%, P \u0026lt; .003). The diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) was established in 17 patients, all of whom had positive ANA test results. Other rheumatic diseases were found in an additional 22 patients. The estimated sensitivity and specificity of the ANA test for SLE were 100% and 86%, respectively. For other rheumatic diseases, sensitivity and specificity were 42% and 85%, respectively. The positive predictive value of the ANA test was 11% for SLE and 11% for other rheumatic diseases. Specificity and positive predictive value for ANA testing in the elderly patients were lower than among younger patients\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EConclusions\u003C\/b\u003E: sensitivity of the ANA test for SLE was high, but overall the positive predictive value was low for SLE or other rheumatic diseases. Sensitivity was low for ANA testing among patients with non-SLE rheumatic disease. More selective test ordering might improve the clinical utility of this test. Clinicians ordering the ANA test should be aware of the test's low-positive predictive value in settings with a low prevalence of rheumatic disease, particularly among older patients.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/8678710\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/8678710\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 2) \u003C\/b\u003EPlease go through the two thesis presentations below and answer the questions below by also discussing them with the presenters:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/youtu.be\/sw8o8y5Yw_I\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/youtu.be\/sw8o8y5Yw_I\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ea) What\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;was the research question in the above thesis presentation?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__To study the association of serum magnesium levels of type 2 diabetes mellitus\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Eb)\u003C\/b\u003E What was the researcher's hypothesis?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__Normal magnesium levels are 1.6 to 2.4\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhere as in diabetics substantial amount of population have a low magnesium levels in the blood, also in non diabetic populations, a low magnesium level is a danger sign that the person might develop diabetes mellitus\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMagnesium deficiency is associated with hypocalcemia, hypokalemia and arrhythmias and hence correlates with a higher mortality \/morbidity\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;If There is reduced serum magnesium they have a negative impact on glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity,leading to early development of complications such as nephropathy,neuropathy and retinopathy and thus have worst outcomes compared to people who are diabetic and have normal magnesium levels.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe diabetic complications progress faster in these populations\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ec) \u003C\/b\u003EWhat is the current available evidence for magnesium deficiency leading to poorer outcomes in patients with diabetes?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__Hypomagnesemia occurs at an incidence of 13.5 to 47.7% among patients with type 2 diabetes. Poor dietary intake, autonomic dysfunction, altered insulin metabolism, glomerular hyperfiltration, osmotic diuresis, recurrent metabolic acidosis, hypophosphatemia, and hypokalemia may be contributory. Hypomagnesemia has been linked to poor glycemic control, coronary artery diseases, hypertension, diabetic retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, and foot ulcerations. The increased incidence of hypomagnesemia among patients with type 2 diabetes presumably is multifactorial. Because current data suggest adverse outcomes in association with hypomagnesemia, it is prudent to monitor magnesium routinely in this patient population and treat the condition whenever possible.”\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;In addition to hyperosmolar coma and ketoacidosis, patients with type 2 diabetes may have cardiovascular disease, nephropathy, retinopathy, and polyneuropathy. With its associated complications, diabetes was reported to be the sixth leading cause of death. numerous studies have reported an inverse relationship between glycemic control and serum Mg levels. In patients with type 2 diabetes, oral Mg supplementation during a 16-wk period was suggested to improve insulin sensitivity and metabolic control\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;There is a correlation between glycemic control and serum Mg levels or improvement of diabetic control with Mg replacement\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECardiovascular.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn a study that involved 19 normotensive individuals without diabetes, 17 hypertensive individuals without diabetes, and 6 hypertensive individuals with diabetes, Resnick et al. documented the lowest mean intracellular Mg concentration among the last group. Similarly, based on data from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study, a multicenter, prospective cohort study that lasted 4 to 7 yr and involved 13,922 middle-aged adults who were free of coronary heart disease at baseline, an inverse association between serum Mg and the risk for coronary heart disease was observed among men with diabetes\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiabetic Retinopathy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe link between hypomagnesemia and diabetic retinopathy was reported in two cross-sectional studies that involved both “insulin-dependent” patients and patients with type 2 diabetes. Not only did patients with diabetes have lower serum Mg levels compared with their counterparts without diabetes, but also the serum Mg levels among the cohort with diabetes had an inverse correlation with the degree of retinopathy .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFoot Ulcerations.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGiven the link between hypomagnesemia and risk factors for the development of diabetic foot ulcers (e.g., polyneuropathy, platelet dysfunction), Rodriguez-Moran and Guerrero-Romero (48) suggested that hypomagnesemia may be associated with an increased risk of diabetic foot ulcers. Indeed, they observed a higher incidence of hypomagnesemia among their patients with diabetic foot ulcers compared with those without the condition (93.9% of the 33 patients with diabetic foot ulcers compared with 73.1% of the 66 patients without diabetic foot ulcers; P = 0.02).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENephropathy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn a comparative study that involved 30 patients who had type 2 diabetes without microalbuminuria, 30 with microalbuminuria, and 30 with overt proteinuria, Corsonello et al. (49) observed a significant decrease in serum ionized Mg in both the microalbuminuria and overt proteinuria groups compared with the nonmicroalbuminuric group. Accordingly, in a recent retrospective study, an association between low serum Mg levels and a significantly faster rate of renal function deterioration in patients with type 2 diabetes was reported (7).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOthers.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFinally, there also are data to suggest the association between hypomagnesemia and other diabetic complications, including dyslipidemia and neurologic abnormalities.Because hypomagnesemia has been linked to various micro- and macrovascular complications, a better understanding of Mg metabolism and efforts to minimize hypomagnesemia in the routine management of diabetes are warranted.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Source:\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/cjasn.asnjournals.org\/content\/2\/2\/366\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/cjasn.asnjournals.org\/content\/2\/2\/366\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/youtu.be\/jXVS5J1-RNE\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/youtu.be\/jXVS5J1-RNE\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ed)\u003C\/b\u003E What was the research question in the above thesis presentation?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__ to analyse the 24 hour urinary sodium with respect to stages of hypertension\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003ETo study effects of sodium on BMI\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003Eanalyse 24 hour urinary sodium excretion in complications of hypertension which include opthalmic,renal and cardiovascular changes.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ee)\u003C\/b\u003E What was the researcher's hypothesis?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__ Researcher wanted to find out whether salt restriction in hypertensive patients,as hgave some sort of benefit to them,but in reality there are two categories of patients salt sensitive\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eand insensitive groups.It is estimated that 50-60% are salt sensitive and only the sensitive group reacts to changes in dietary salt intake with alterations in blood pressure. It is estimated that about 50-60 % of hypertensives are salt sensitive.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;f)\u003C\/b\u003E What is the current available evidence for the utility of monitoring salt excretion in the hypertensive population?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__ High dietary intake of sodium is seen in most of the subjects who have very high blood pressures\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBy the means of a self monitoring device\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESubjects were 34 hypertensive patients who underwent successful 24-h home urine collection five times and 25 volunteers. Four volunteers were diagnosed as having hypertension based on home blood pressure (BP) readings. All subjects were asked to measure daily urinary salt excretion for 30 days by using a self-monitoring device which estimates 24-h salt excretion by overnight urine. The mean urinary salt excretion during the 30 days was 8.36 +\/- 1.52 g\/day and the range (maximum-minimum value) was 5.47 +\/- 20.05 g\/day in all subjects. Mean urinary salt excretion decreased from 8.52 +\/- 1.63 g\/day for the first 10 days to 8.31 +\/- 1.54 g\/day for the last 10 days (p \u0026lt; 0.05). The mean urinary salt excretion determined by a self-monitoring device using overnight urine was positively associated with that determined by 24-h home urine for five times in the hypertensive subjects (r = 0.63, p \u0026lt; 0.01). Results indicate that a self-monitoring device seems to be useful to monitor daily salt intake and to guide salt restriction.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis might be useful in subjects who are sensitive to sodium restriction\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/20001461\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/20001461\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 3)\u003C\/b\u003E Please critically appraise the full text article linked below:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-2796.2003.01233.x\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-2796.2003.01233.x\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhat is the efficacy of aspirin in stroke in your assessment of the evidence provided in the article. Please go through the RCT CASP checklist here https:\/\/casp-uk.net\/casp-tools-checklists\/ and answer the questions mentioned in the checklist in relation to your article.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__The study was to know the efficacy of asprin for prevention of stroke progression.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__the participants and the investigators were blind methodically\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__there were dropouts in the study, study medication was interrupted in few due to suspected side effects.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__the treatment effect wasn't much,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__the outcomes are benefial to the population in prescribing anticoagulants\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 4)\u003C\/b\u003E Please mention your individual learning experiences from this month.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__ performed a mini mental status examination and tried to elicit the cause of delirium in a patient, cause is a chronic ulcer due to which RFT is deranged and high creatinine levels.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__salt and fluid restriction in a maintainence hemodialysis patient and outcomes in the long run\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__learnt about osmotic demyelination syndrome in a pt of\u0026nbsp; hyponatremia\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__learnt about cardiorenal syndrome\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__ learnt about viral\u0026nbsp; hepatitis, jaundice\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__ examined a pt of stroke and leanrt how to reach to the site of lesion\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 5) a) \u003C\/b\u003EWhat are the possible reasons for the 36 year old man's hypertension and CAD described in the link below since three years?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-2796.2003.01233.x\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-2796.2003.01233.x\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__The patient is a chronic alcoholic and smoker since 15 years\u0026nbsp; and as nicotine acts as a vasoconstrictor in the long run, this is the main reason for his hypertension\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Eb)\u003C\/b\u003E Please describe the ECG changes and correlate them with the patient's current diagnosis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E__Ecg shows normal axis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBut there is an irregularly irregular rhythm\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd also there are intermittent broad QRS complexes\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAlso there is a poor R wave progression but the rhythm in the remaining ecgs seems to be regular\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ec)\u003C\/b\u003E Share an RCT that provides evidence for the efficacy of primary PTCA in acute myocardial infarction over medical management. Describe the efficacy in a PICO format.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E__Objectives\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe Air Primary Angioplasty in Myocardial Infarction(PAMI) study was designed to determine the best reperfusion strategy for patients with high-risk acute myocardial infarction (AMI) at hospitals without percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty(PTCA) capability.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPrevious studies have suggested that high-risk patients have better outcomes with primary PTCA than with thrombolytic therapy. It is unknown whether this advantage would be lost if the patient had to be transferred for PTCA, and reperfusion was delayed\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMethods\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatients with high-risk AMI (age \u0026gt;70 years, anterior MI, Killip class II\/III, heart rate \u0026gt;100 beats\/min or systolic BP \u0026lt;100 mm Hg) who were eligible for thrombolytic therapy were randomized to either transfer for primary PTCA or on-site thrombolysis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EResults\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOne hundred thirty-eight patients were randomized before the study ended (71 to transfer for PTCA and 67 to thrombolysis). The time from arrival to treatment was delayed in the transfer group (155 vs. 51 min, p \u0026lt; 0.0001), largely due to the initiation of transfer (43 min) and transport time (26 min). Patients randomized to transfer had a reduced hospital stay (6.1 ± 4.3 vs. 7.5 ± 4.3 days, p = 0.015) and less ischemia (12.7% vs. 31.8%, p = 0.007). At 30 days, a 38% reduction in major adverse cardiac events was observed for the transfer group; however, because of the inability to recruit the necessary sample size, this did not achieve statistical significance (8.4% vs. 13.6%, p = 0.331).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EConclusions\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatients with high-risk AMI at hospitals without a catheterization laboratory may have an improved outcome when transferred for primary PTCA versus on-site thrombolysis; however, this will require further study. The marked delay in the transfer process suggests a role for triaging patients directly to specialized heart-attack centers.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESource\u003C\/b\u003E:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca A 55 year old man with Recurrent Focal Seizures\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDetailed patient case report here:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/ushaindurthi.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-with-complaints-of.html\"\u003Ehttp:\/\/ushaindurthi.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-with-complaints-of.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. What is the problem representation of this patient and what could be the anatomical site of lesion ?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 55 year old male maestri(who builds houses)with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus who is a chronic alcoholic \u0026amp; smoker came with c\/o weakness of right upper limb with involuntary movements of both right upper limb and lower limb.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2. Why are subcortical internal capsular infarcts more common that cortical infarcts?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003ESubcortical infarcts are caused because of the minute branches of main arteries supplying the subcortex\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;rather than cortical\u0026nbsp; area which is supplied by major artery\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3. What is the pathogenesis involved in cerebral infarct related seizures?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EInfarct causes hypoxia which causes imbalanced electrical activity in the brain which leads to seizures.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4. What is your take on the ecg? And do you agree with the treating team on starting the patient on Enoxaparin?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cb\u003EECG\u003C\/b\u003E: \u003C\/u\u003EThere is RBBB\u0026nbsp;with LEFT AXIS DEVIATION seen in the Ecg.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESinus tachycardia noted in the intital Ecg.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPoor R wave progression can be seen.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EYes\u003C\/b\u003E I agree with the treating team on starting the patient on Enoxaparin.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; Because Enoxoparin is given post stroke to prevent the emboli from travelling to the heart or lungs and thus helps in preventing cardiac arrest or pulmonary embolism.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E5. Which AED would you prefer?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EI would prefer carbamazepine.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIf so why?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBecause it is drug of choice for focal seizures.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECarbamazepine and phenytoin are drugs of choice in initial monotherapy for adult partial and secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures. These designations reflect the results of the Veterans Administration Epilepsy Cooperative Study Group of 1985. An earlier comparative study of carbamazepine and phenytoin by Ramsay and associates found both drugs equally effective in controlling new-onset seizures. Among the \u003Cb\u003Eadvantages of carbamazepine is that it causes relatively few cognitive and dysmorphic side effects\u003C\/b\u003E. Its disadvantages are its unavailability in parenteral formulation and its metabolic autoinduction. The latter must be compensated for by planned dosage increases to maintain therapeutic plasma steady-state levels during the first 2 or 3 months of treatment.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 2) 55 year old man with Recurrent hypoglycemia\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/manojkumar1008.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/shortness-of-breath-with-high-sugars.html\"\u003Ehttp:\/\/manojkumar1008.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/shortness-of-breath-with-high-sugars.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. What is the problem representation for this patient?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EA 55 year old male with Type 2 Diabetes mellitus with c\/o dyspnea on exertion and cough since 3 days and sudden onset of giddiness and profuse sweating secondary to Oral hypoglycemic agents induced hypoglycemia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2. What is the cause for his recurrent hypoglycemia? And how would you evaluate?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EThe oral hypoglycemic agent (glimiperide ) isn't getting excreted due to decreased functioning of the kidney. What is the pathogenesis involved in hypoglycemia ?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;The\u0026nbsp;hormone insulin lowers blood sugar levels when blood sugar is too high. If you have type 1 or type 2 diabetes and need insulin to control your blood sugar, taking more insulin than you need can cause your blood sugar level to drop too low and result in hypoglycemia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E5. Do you agree with the treating team on starting the patient on antibiotics? And why? Mention the efficacies for the treatment given.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EYes i agree with the treating team starting the patient on antibiotics as his renal parameters are deranged. So it might help the recovery of the kidney.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 3)A\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;41 year old man with Polyarthralgia\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECase details here: \u003C\/b\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/mahathireddybandari.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/41m-with-chest-pain-and-joint-pains.html?m=1\" style=\"font-weight: bold;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/mahathireddybandari.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/41m-with-chest-pain-and-joint-pains.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. What are their efficacies?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EYes i\u0026nbsp;agree with the treatment provided by the treating team\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELasix \u0026amp; Nebulization : For wheezing and crepts\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/jamanetwork.com\/journals\/jamaneurology\/fullarticle\/787258\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/jamanetwork.com\/journals\/jamaneurology\/fullarticle\/787258\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELactulose : for liver problems\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EZofer : to control nausea and vomitings\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPantop : To prevent gastric irritation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 4) 60 year woman with Uncontrolled sugars\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/manojkumar1008.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/60-yr-old-female-with-uncontrolled.html\"\u003Ehttp:\/\/manojkumar1008.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/60-yr-old-female-with-uncontrolled.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. What is the problem representation of this patient?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;A\u0026nbsp;60 year old female with Type 2\u0026nbsp; Diabetes Mellitus with c\/o pricking type of chest pain since 4 days and uncontrolled sugars secondary to ? right upper lobe pneumonic consolidation with sepsis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2. What are the factors contributing to her uncontrolled blood sugars?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EToo much food, such as a meal or snack with more carbohydrates than usual.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENot being active.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENot enough insulin or oral diabetes medications.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESide effects from other medications, such as steroids or antipsychotic medications.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3. What are the chest xray findings?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003ETrachea shifted towards right\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EConsolidation is seen in the right upper lobe.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4. What do you think is the cause for her hypoalbuminaemia? How would you approach it?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u0026nbsp; \u003C\/b\u003Ecause :\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003EMalnutrition\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; Protein loss from urine\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;Less protein diet\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cu\u003EApproach:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"text-decoration-line: underline;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/lh3.googleusercontent.com\/-3Y3LK6FmdDM\/X9r48FI-CII\/AAAAAAAABf0\/d-7DrTYUDMQlGmMk5knN7khvIlc6oJ16wCLcBGAsYHQ\/s1600\/1608186086020978-0.png\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/lh3.googleusercontent.com\/-3Y3LK6FmdDM\/X9r48FI-CII\/AAAAAAAABf0\/d-7DrTYUDMQlGmMk5knN7khvIlc6oJ16wCLcBGAsYHQ\/s1600\/1608186086020978-0.png\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E- by advising the pt to take protien powder with milk ,also to eat egg whites... basically advising the pt to eat protien rich food .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E5. Comment on the treatment given along with each of their efficacies with supportive evidence.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EPiptaz \u0026amp; clarithromycin : antibiotics for consolidation\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEgg white \u0026amp; protien powder : To replenish protein\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELactulose : to relieve constipation\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EActrapid (HAI): to control hyperglycemia\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETramadol : to relieve her pain\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPantop : to prevent gastritis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EZofer : to prevent nausea and\u0026nbsp; vomitings\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 5) 56 year old man with Decompensated liver disease\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECase report here:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/appalaaishwaryareddy.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/56year-old-male-with-decompensated.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/appalaaishwaryareddy.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/56year-old-male-with-decompensated.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. What is the anatomical and pathological localization of the problem?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u003C\/b\u003E56 year old male who is a known case of CLD and hepatitis B postive presented with the complaints of abdominal distension since 3months with yellowish discoloration of eyes since 3months and shortness of breath since 2days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELocalization of the problem\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eknown case of liver disease with hepatitis B positive with pancytopenia\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EKidney injury - With Elevated Serum creatinine and blood urea and refractory hyperkalemia\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHis ABG shows Metabolic Acidosis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELUNGS - pleural effusion\u0026nbsp; in right side\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2. alt=\"\"\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3. What is the pathogenesis of the illness due to Hepatitis B?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u003C\/b\u003EThe pathogenesis and clinical manifestations of hepatitis B are due to the interaction of the virus and the host immune system, which leads to liver injury and, potentially, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Patients can have either an acute symptomatic disease or an asymptomatic disease.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4. Is it necessary to have a separate haemodialysis set up for hepatits B patients and why?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;Not necessarily , because the dialysis machines are well disinfected after every dialysis and it's tubes are also disposable ,so chances of spreading virus through hemodialysis machine are nil to very minimal .. Hence my answer is no\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E5. What are the efficacies of each treatment given to this patient? Describe the efficacies with supportive RCT evidence.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn the last years, marked progress has been made in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B. The efficacy of lamivudine, the first nucleoside analogue available, is limited by the high incidence of resistance. Adefovir, which was recently approved has a comparable efficacy with a very low frequency of resistance. However, adefovir needs to be indefinitely administered as withdrawal of therapy is generally associated with reactivation and sustained response is uncommon. Recent large randomized controlled trials showed that PEG IFNs induce relatively high sustained response rates both in HBeAg positive and HBeAg negative chronic hepatitis B. So far, the combination of PEG IFN with lamivudine, used simultaneously, is disappointing in terms of short-term efficacy. However, long-term efficacy needs to be assessed and different schedules of combination (for example sequential) need to be evaluated. A number of nucleoside analogues, with favourable toxicity profiles and a promise of increased effectiveness against HBV, are at various stages of clinical development. Results of phase III trials of entecavir and emtricitabine confirmed their efficacy. However, while entecavir is associated with a low incidences of resistance, emtricitabine is associated with a relatively high incidence of resistance which limits its use as a monotherapy. The efficacy and safety of new and more potent drugs like telbivudine and clevudine need to be confirmed. The future of chronic hepatitis B therapy seems to be in the combination of different drugs. Ideally, the optimal drugs to combine would meet the following criteria: they should have different sites of action on HBV DNA replication, a potent antiviral effect, an excellent safety profile and they should induce a sustained response with a limited duration of therapy. Indeed, the concept of combination therapy has been recently developed in order to increase efficacy and to decrease the occurrence of viral resistance. However, so far few combinations have been evaluated. No combination therapy demonstrated a benefit as compared with monotherapy. More potent drugs and new combinations together with the understanding of the mechanisms of resistance to therapy are important challenges to improve the efficacy of treatment and decrease in the future the global burden related to chronic hepatitis B.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 6) 58 year old man with Dementia\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/jabeenahmed300.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/this-is-online-e-log-book-to-discuss.html\"\u003Ehttp:\/\/jabeenahmed300.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/this-is-online-e-log-book-to-discuss.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. What is the problem representation of this patient?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EA 58 year old weaver by occupation, alcoholic 20.years back with c\/o slurring of speech , deviation of mouth to right side associated with drooling of saliva , food particles and water predominantly from left angle of mouth and smacking of lips since 6 months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUrinary urge incontinence since 6 months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EForgetfulness since 3 months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe has delayed response to commands.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDysphagia to both solids and liquids since 10 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiagnosed with CVA 3 years back and now he was diagnosed as neuro degenerative disease - Alzheimer's\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2. alt=\"\"\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3. Do you think his dementia could be explained by chronic infarcts?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003EMultiinfarct dementia(MID)is caused by a series of small strokes. A stroke, or infarct, is the interruption or blockage of blood flow to any part of the brain. The term “multi-infarct” means many strokes and many areas of damage. If blood flow is stopped for more than a few seconds, brain cells can die from a lack of oxygen. This damage is usually permanent.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA stroke can be silent, which means it affects such a small area of the brain that it goes unnoticed. Over time, many silent strokes can lead to MID. Are you aware of pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions to treat such a patient and what are their known efficacies based on RCT evidence?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EPHARMACOLOGIC:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003ECholinesterase inhibitors\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E:\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDonepezil\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEfficacy of starting of donezepil in early stage Alzheimer's to improve cognitive function.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/jamanetwork.com\/journals\/jamaneurology\/fullarticle\/787258\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/jamanetwork.com\/journals\/jamaneurology\/fullarticle\/787258\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERivastigmine\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGalantamine\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Ci\u003ENON PHARMACOLOGIC\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECounselling the patient and care givers\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGeriatric care\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQuestion 7) 22 year old man with seizures\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECase report here\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/geethagugloth.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/a-22-year-old-with-seizures.html\"\u003Ehttp:\/\/geethagugloth.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/a-22-year-old-with-seizures.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. What is the problem representation of this patient ? What is the anatomic and pathologic localization in view of the clinical and radiological findings?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003EA 22 year old delivery boy chronic alcoholic and tobacco chewer with c\/o on \u0026amp; off fever since 1 year , involuntary weight loss since 6 months , headache since 2 months , 4 - 5 episodes of involuntary stiffening of both Upperlimb \u0026amp; Lowerlimb with 5 mins of\u0026nbsp; LOC one week before the day of admission.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBrain - multiple ring enhancing lesions in right cerebellum\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E? Tuberculoma\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2. What the your differentials to his ring enhancing lesions?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA:\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;HIV\/AIDS\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;toxoplasmosis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;fungal infections such as cryptococcosis or histoplasmosis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eprimary brain tumors\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Emetastases\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;brain abscesses\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;granulomas\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eresolving hematomas\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Einfarcts\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3. What is \"immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome IRIS and how was this patient's treatment modified to avoid the possibility of his developing it?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA: \u003C\/b\u003EImmune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) describes a collection of inflammatory disorders associated with paradoxical worsening of preexisting infectious processes following the initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART) in HIV-infected individuals\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAwaiting for CD4 count to modify treatment.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;8) Please mention your individual learning experiences from this month.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-One day while attending rounds,I have learnt a very interesting and important point that oral hypoglycemic drugs should not be given to a diabetic pt who has renal failure or improper renal function. As the drug won't get excreted, the pt will suffer from hypoglycemia(which is due to prolonged effect of the OHA).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-Also learnt that nor-adrenaline infusion shouldn't be stopped at a time, it should be slowly tapered, else the pt will get collapsed.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have learnt ECG basics .Able to identify bundle blocks and st elevations , R wave progression etc\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have learnt how to diagnose a pt with DKA and also it's management.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have learnt that the drugs should be prescribed based on their efficacies in the treatment .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have seen many hypertensive patients and their management .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have seen heart failure cases and the approach to them.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have seen pateints with seizures and the treatment which we give to them.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have seen patients with stroke(CVA) , assisted in examining the pts.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have tried to identify infarcts in the radiological films.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have seen that the resting tremors of parkinsonism can be stopped for a small period of time by deliberately moving the body part.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- I have learnt to read and assess ABG report.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have studied abt aphasias\u0026nbsp; especially broca's and wernickie\u0026nbsp; and how the pt will present to the hospital.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-learnt adjustment of Insulin doses according to GRBS levels.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I gave HAI subcutaneously to a patient.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-Perfomed CPR.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have seen a patient\u0026nbsp; with recurrent episodes of\u0026nbsp; seizures and the seizures weren't getting subsided by mutiple doses of antiepileptic drugs and so learnt that the end choice was to\u0026nbsp; intubate the pt and to put on a ventilator for a period of time.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- I have seen 2d echo perfomed on patients and tried to\u0026nbsp; learn the assessment of ventricular contractility and valvular function.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- I have seen endoscopic view of upper GIT in the gastroenterology superspeciality.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-Have studied Neuroanatomy a little.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-I have auscultated and got to know the difference between crepts and wheeze.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/jabeenahmed300.blogspot.com\/feeds\/5023982381383499257\/comments\/default","title":"Post Comments"},{"rel":"replies","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/jabeenahmed300.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/exam.html#comment-form","title":"0 Comments"},{"rel":"edit","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/4439497073862043557\/posts\/default\/5023982381383499257"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/4439497073862043557\/posts\/default\/5023982381383499257"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/jabeenahmed300.blogspot.com\/2020\/12\/exam.html","title":"BIMONTHLY EXAM FOR THE MONTH OF DECEMBER 2020"}],"author":[{"name":{"$t":"JABEEN"},"uri":{"$t":"http:\/\/www.blogger.com\/profile\/18234611839507615576"},"email":{"$t":"noreply@blogger.com"},"gd$image":{"rel":"http://schemas.google.com/g/2005#thumbnail","width":"16","height":"16","src":"https:\/\/img1.blogblog.com\/img\/b16-rounded.gif"}}],"media$thumbnail":{"xmlns$media":"http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/","url":"https:\/\/lh3.googleusercontent.com\/-3Y3LK6FmdDM\/X9r48FI-CII\/AAAAAAAABf0\/d-7DrTYUDMQlGmMk5knN7khvIlc6oJ16wCLcBGAsYHQ\/s72-c\/1608186086020978-0.png","height":"72","width":"72"},"thr$total":{"$t":"0"}}]}}
